html:
The Meherrin are an Iroquoian-speaking people of the Northeastern Woodlands who lived along the Meherrin River, between the Piedmont and the coastal plain on the border of Virginia and North Carolina.

Their closest relatives were the Nottoway and the Tuscarora, fellow Iroquoian speakers surrounded by Algonquian and Siouan peoples. English settlers from Virginia pressed onto their lands from the later 1600s. Many Meherrin went north and joined the Haudenosaunee Confederacy; they later fled the American army's Sullivan Expedition of 1779 and settled in Canada on the Six Nations of the Grand River. Others stayed in North Carolina, where the Meherrin Indian Tribe is recognised by the state.
sum: The Meherrin are an Iroquoian-speaking people of the Northeastern Woodlands who lived along the Meherrin River, between the Piedmont and the coastal plain on the border of Virginia and North Carolina.
